extracted.intended_audience: NLP and XAI researchers and practitioners working on clickbait detection, dataset creators, and content-moderation engineers
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, training, and evaluating systems that (1) detect whether a news headline is clickbait and (2) attribute which specific persuasive/linguistic tactics produced the clickbait effect, using synthetic augmentation and explainability methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curiosity Gap
rubrics_metrics.description: Withholding key information to provoke curiosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect patterns that omit crucial WHO/WHAT/WHERE details (e.g., 'You will never guess…', forward-reference phrases like 'this', 'someone') and label headlines that intentionally leave out specifics to create a gap. Used as a distinct tactic label in multi-label attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exaggeration and Hyperbole
rubrics_metrics.description: Overstating claims to increase perceived importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag sensational intensifiers and hyperbolic adjectives (e.g., 'insane', 'shocking', 'stunning', 'very best', 'absolutely') and typographic emphasis (ALL CAPS, repeated punctuation). These cues indicate exaggeration as a manipulation tactic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional Triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: Using emotionally charged language to elicit strong reactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify language intended to evoke fear, outrage, awe, or pity (e.g., 'heartbreaking', 'you'll cry'). Treat presence of strong affective words as a tactic label and prioritize features capturing sentiment and emotion-laden lexicons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensationalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Framing ordinary events as shocking or extraordinary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for framing that magnifies mundane facts into dramatic claims. Related to exaggeration but emphasizes reframing rather than only lexical intensifiers. Useful to distinguish from legitimate urgency in news headlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lists and Superlatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilizing list structures or superlatives to attract attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect listicle forms ('10 Secrets…', 'Top 5…') and superlative constructions ('best', 'most') as explicit engagement tactics. Typically straightforward binary features (is listicle? is superlative?).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguous References
rubrics_metrics.description: Using vague entities to create intrigue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark deictic or forward-reference expressions ('this', 'here', 'that person') that avoid naming subjects. These create uncertainty that drives clicks and are part of the Curiosity Gap family but treated here as its own detectable pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct Appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Addressing the reader directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect second-person pronouns ('you'), imperatives ('watch this now'), colloquial tone or slang. These stylistic signals produce intimacy or urgency and can be used as a tactic label in attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfinished Narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: Implies a story but leaves out the conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify teaser constructions that promise an unresolved story ('...but the next move?','This will change your life'). These are structural patterns that withhold conclusions to induce clicks; label as a tactic in multi-label outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unexpected Associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Juxtaposing unrelated concepts to spark curiosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect unusual or surprising conceptual pairings that imply novelty or a twist. Use semantic anomaly detectors or association features to find these tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provocative Questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Using open or rhetorical questions to engage the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag question-form headlines that are rhetorical or invite guessing ('Can you guess what happened next?'). Treat presence of such questions as an explicit tactic feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linguistic cues and hand-crafted features for clickbait
rubrics_metrics.description: Surface-level linguistic indicators historically used for clickbait detection (e.g., punctuation patterns, forward-reference words, superlatives, POS tags, unusual punctuation like excessive '!' or '?').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include binary/continuous features for punctuation counts, presence of teaser words ('this', 'someone'), POS-based patterns, stop-word ratios, and specific n-grams; these features help interpretable baselines and illuminate model decision drivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset composition: annotated original + clickbait variants + tactic labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Each sample must include the original non-clickbait headline, one or more clickbait-augmented variants, and the exact set of tactics used for augmentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This composition supports both binary detection training and multi-label tactic attribution. Ensure broad topical coverage and retain original-to-augmented mappings for controlled evaluation and ablation studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthetic data generation via controlled augmentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate clickbait variants by systematically applying predefined tactics (via prompts or transformation rules) to real headlines, using LLMs (e.g., GPT-4o) with prompts that specify which tactic(s) to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully craft prompts to enforce target tactics, annotate each generated sample with the applied tactic set, and validate quality via human inspection to avoid spurious distributional artifacts. Balance diversity with fidelity to real-world style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics for detection and attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Use precision, recall, F1-score (and accuracy for detection) to measure both binary clickbait detection and multi-label tactic attribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report precision, recall, F1 by model and setting (zero-shot, few-shot, fine-tuned). For multi-label attribution report overall precision/recall/F1 and per-class metrics to capture ability to distinguish overlapping techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of explanation quality and faithfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether generated explanations truthfully reflect model reasoning and align with human-identified evidence (e.g., fidelity, precision@k, NDCG for rationale retrieval).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use metrics like fidelity (does removing highlighted features reduce confidence?), precision@k/NDCG against human rationales, and human evaluation studies to measure clarity and usefulness for moderators/end-users. Recognize that LLM explanations can be plausible but unfaithful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation and attribution methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods to produce interpretable attributions include post-hoc feature attribution (LIME, SHAP), attention/rationale extraction, co-attention over content and comments, and LLM-generated natural-language explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select methods based on desired interpretability/faithfulness trade-off: SHAP/LIME for feature importance, attention/rationale models for extractive highlights, and LLMs for free-text rationales—validate each method's reliability via quantitative (fidelity, NDCG) and human evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-stage pipeline evaluation (detection then attribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate the task into: (1) a detection stage that classifies headlines as clickbait or not, and (2) an attribution stage that identifies the present tactics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate both stages independently and jointly. Pipelines can combine a fine-tuned detector with a BERT-based multi-label classifier for attribution, or use LLMs for one or both stages; report detection accuracy and attribution precision/recall/F1 separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompting strategy: zero-shot vs few-shot (tactic-aware exemplars)
rubrics_metrics.description: LLM performance varies by prompting: zero-shot uses only instructions; few-shot includes labeled exemplars (especially tactic-aware exemplars) which can improve detection and direct tactic prediction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiment with tactic-aware few-shot exemplars in prompts to boost LLM attribution performance; measure how few-shot examples change F1/precision/recall compared to zero-shot and to supervised baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution model design: dedicated BERT multi-label classifier vs LLM direct attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribution can be produced by a dedicated supervised multi-label BERT classifier or directly by LLMs prompted to predict tactics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supervised BERT multi-label component provides stable multi-label predictions when annotated data is available; LLM direct attribution can work with few-shot prompts but may be less accurate—compare approaches on attribution precision, recall, and interpretability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade-offs: accuracy, interpretability, and computational/deployment cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Design choices should be evaluated in terms of detection accuracy, clarity/faithfulness of explanations, and computational and deployment complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fine-tuned PLMs (e.g., BERT) often yield highest detection F1 but require labeled data and compute; LLMs offer zero-shot/few-shot convenience and flexible natural-language explanations but may be less accurate and more costly to run. Report these trade-offs and choose architecture aligned with deployment constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimodal and contextual signals for robust detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate article content, thumbnail images, and social context (clicks, shares, comments) as signals when available to improve detection and explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multimodal mismatch (image unrelated to headline) and propagation metadata can indicate clickbait but may detect only after spread. Use multimodal models or causal disentangling techniques to separate intrinsic bait content from irrelevant signals, balancing early detection needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-resource and generalization strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Address data scarcity through augmentation (LLM-generated, paraphrasing), adversarial/semi-supervised generation, contrastive learning, and cross-lingual PLMs for low-resource languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate synthetic and adversarial samples via human review to avoid artifacts; use contrastive methods and multilingual PLMs (mBERT, XLM) to transfer knowledge; weight synthetic vs real samples carefully to improve real-world generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-in-the-loop evaluation for explanation usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure whether explanations are clear and actionable to moderators and end-users through user studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond automatic faithfulness metrics, conduct human evaluation to assess clarity, usefulness, and whether explanations increase trust or understanding. Use these results to iterate on explanation format (extractive highlights vs natural-language rationales).
